newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ parliament sets up FEC committee.
newsitem.headline: NZ parliament sets up FEC committee.

text.p: Parliament on Wednesday set up the powerful finance and expenditure select committee with its 12 members drawn evenly from the government and the opposition.

But with representatives of free-market Act New Zealand and centrist United on the committee, it is likely to endorse the National-New Zealand First coalition government's centre-right economic direction.
Select committees examine proposed legislation and government departments' performance. They can initiate their own inquiries.

The members of the finance and expenditure committee are: Tony Ryall, Belinda Vernon, Marie Hasler and David Carter from National, Doug Woolerton and Jenny Bloxham from New Zealand First, Rodney Hide from Act, Peter Dunne from United, John Wright from the Alliance and Michael Cullen, Ruth Dyson and Mark Peck from Labour.
The committee mewmbers will elect the chairperson, which is tipped to go to National's Tony Ryall.

Parliament began debating motions to set up the 17 committees on Tuesday in the face of objections from the opposition Labour and Alliance parties who believe they should have four committee chairpersons between them.

The government and Act have reached an understanding which will see Act MP Derek Quigley chair the foreign affairs and defence committee. In return, Act will back National's nominations for other chairpersonships.
Labour is likely to chair only one committee, regulations review, which has traditionally gone to the opposition.
